results.question: How should I practise these bars?
results.answer: 1. Count it: Say the count for bars 7–8 out loud: 1 e & a 2 e & a 3 e & a 4 e & a | 1 e & a 2 e & a 3 e & a 4 e & a Done when: Count the whole passage twice without a pause. 2. Slow at 60 BPM: Play bars 7–8 slowly with the metronome. Done when: Play it 3 times in a row without stopping or missing a note. 3. Loop at 80 BPM: Loop bars 7–8 at a medium tempo. Done when: Play it 4 times in a row without stopping or missing a note. 4. Connect at 80 BPM: Add one bar before and one bar after bars 7–8. Done when: Play it 2 times in a row without stopping or missing a note. 5. Full tempo at 100 BPM: Play bars 7–8 at the score's tempo. Done when: Play it 3 times in a row without stopping or missing a note.

results.question: Find the most complex part
results.answer: The busiest notation is in bars 7–8 (notation score 50 out of 100): 16 hits, down to 16th notes, kick or hi-hat pedal together with another drum on 6 of 16 hits and 8 hits on "e", "a" or triplet counts rather than the beat or "&". This is about how busy the notes are, not how hard they will feel for you.
